title: Halcyon customization system — concept and staged plan
purpose: Choose a complete desktop, change it visually, make personal components, and share the result.
existing_foundation: Widget data providers and live tools
Theme families, wallpaper colours and shared/per-surface materials
Setups with domain selection, import/export, schedules, Apply and Undo
Multi-display widget placement and optional Islands

system_model.meaning: A portable composition of wallpaper, style, widget instances, layout rules and optional dock/panel preferences.
Named colours, typography, spacing, corner shapes, borders and surface treatment. Each component can Follow setup or keep an explicit override.
A reusable presentation assembled from text, images, icons, meters and layout containers, bound to existing providers.
A recipe placed on a display, with independent sizing and optional style overrides. Account connections and personal content remain local.
Anchors, groups, spacing and compact/wide variants that adapt to available display area rather than copying physical monitor IDs.
Translate supported choices into native COSMIC theme, font, icon and panel configuration; expose unsupported controls accurately.

interaction_rules: Choose a complete setup; Preview, Apply or Remix.
Click an object on the desktop canvas, or choose it from an equivalent keyboard-accessible list.
Keep Design, Content and Layout separate; visually identify inherited values and overrides.
Preview display changes the canvas being inspected. It does not make global system fonts or colours per-display.
Canvas changes form a setup-scoped draft with Cancel and Apply; preserve existing direct-control semantics elsewhere.
Save widget saves a reusable design; it does not export live notes, accounts or calendar contents.
Missing data has deliberate empty, stale and disconnected states; previews use clearly identified sample data.
Narrow windows show a canvas/inspector switch instead of squeezing three columns.
Islands remain optional; setups retain a standard-panel fallback.

phases.title: Shared styling and first real desktops
deliver: Additive, versioned style and widget-layout schema with migration for existing preferences and setups.
Digital, stacked and analogue clock faces; compact and expanded weather, agenda and music variants.
Implement Tidal and Paper first to prove very different layouts through one renderer; then Moss and Carbon.
Use existing data providers and native panel controls; add only capabilities demonstrated by the first looks.
exit: Real screenshots match agreed composition and hierarchy.
Old setups still import; Apply and Undo preserve content and display assignments.
Readable at 100%, 150% and 200% scaling, light/dark themes and minimum supported sizes.
Record idle/animated CPU, GPU, memory and wakeup measurements against current baseline; choose numeric budgets before extending effects.

phases.title: Desktop canvas editor
deliver: Select, move, resize, group, align and snap objects with inspector controls.
Shared-style editing, per-object overrides, clear inheritance/reset actions.
Display preview, compact/wide layout previews and setup-scoped draft review.
Keyboard alternatives and compact-window inspector navigation.
exit: Tidal can be remixed into a different working desktop without editing a file.
Preview and applied output agree on size, placement and supported native styling.
Cancel/Undo and display disconnect/reconnect retain draft and placement correctness.

phases.title: Personal widget builder
deliver: Start from an existing widget or a small set of templates.
Compose native Text, Time, Date, Icon, Image, Meter, Row and Column parts.
Bind approved data and actions from current Clock, Weather, Calendar, Music and monitoring services.
Save reusable recipes with minimum sizes, compact/wide layouts and explicit missing-data states.
exit: A user can build and reuse the illustrated clock/weather card.
Several recipes share provider subscriptions; hidden widgets do not keep unnecessary work alive.
Recipes remain bounded, accessible, versioned and recoverable on invalid input.

phases.title: Portable sharing and remix
deliver: Extend existing setup import/export with bounded asset bundles, previews, capability requirements and creator/licence metadata.
Export review identifies included domains and excludes secrets, personal content and physical display IDs.
Import preview explains optional dependencies and supports compatible fallbacks.
Add a curated catalogue and stable links after package import/export works; Copy link refers to a published immutable revision.
exit: A setup round-trips between two different display arrangements.
Missing fonts, assets or Islands produce clear fallback previews.
Imported designs cannot run arbitrary commands; package updates never silently replace personal remixes.

phases.title: Community and polish
deliver: Built-in, Mine and Community views with filters, creator credits and local favourites.
Remix lineage, explicit update review, reporting/removal process for hosted contributions.
Improve animation, presets and additional native integrations from measured user feedback.
exit: People can discover, preview, remix and share a desktop through the UI.
Fresh-machine, offline, mixed-display and keyboard acceptance passes.
Gallery operations and large catalogues stay within agreed resource budgets.

boundaries: The seven images are generated concepts, not screenshots of implemented features. Exact dates, app icons, preview content and controls are illustrative.
Four desktop treatments are expressions of one system, not four separately hardcoded widget implementations.
Current profile transport is allowlisted and bounded. Rich packages require an additive format and migration, not relaxing existing import rules.
Settings chrome remains native and readable; desktop components can be expressive.
Real compositor blur, lock-screen replacement and arbitrary shell scripts are outside the initial plan.
A general third-party code plugin system needs a separate design; this first builder composes existing trusted providers.
Artwork, fonts and icon sets need distributable licences before inclusion in shipping presets.
first_deliverable: Two real desktops, Tidal and Paper, using the same new clock/style model with existing data providers, plus measured compact/scaled/Undo acceptance.
archive_notice: Historical proposal. Current architecture and sequencing are in ../../ARCHITECTURE.md, ../../ROADMAP.md and ../../tracker.json.
